amenities.cold_plunge: Victoria's cold plunge culture sits within a broader European bathhouse tradition that has taken hold gradually in Australian cities. Cold immersion pools — maintained well below ambient temperature, typically fed by chilled water systems rather than natural sources — are the point around which many contemporary bathhouse circuits are built. Sense of Self in Collingwood is currently the sole listed venue in this state carrying the amenity.
amenities.magnesium_pool: Magnesium pools use water saturated with magnesium chloride rather than the sodium chloride of seawater or the calcium compounds of hard tap water — the mineral is absorbed transdermally, though the degree of uptake remains a subject of ongoing physiological research. Victoria's listing in this category is currently a single entry: Sense of Self in Collingwood.
amenities.traditional_sauna: Victoria's bathhouse offering with a traditional sauna is, at present, a short list — Sense of Self in Collingwood standing as the single entry. A traditional sauna operates on dry or low-humidity heat, typically wood-fired or electrically heated, distinct from steam rooms or infrared cabinets. Whether the category grows is a matter of record; this page reflects what is documented now.

VIC.state: Victoria's bathhouse culture is modest by international measure, though it has been gathering definition in recent years. Sense of Self in Collingwood currently represents the state's indexed offering — a single venue does not make a tradition, but it marks a starting point from which the category can be tracked over time.
